taxonomy.subtopic: Autoantibodies against BP180/BP230 hemidesmosomal proteins with subepidermal separation

questions.stem_html: An 81-year-old woman has intensely pruritic, tense bullae on the trunk and flexural extremities without oral lesions. Histology shows a subepidermal blister with eosinophils. The accompanying immunofluorescence schematic shows linear IgG and C3 at the basement-membrane zone. Which structure is targeted?

options.text_html: Desmoglein 3 in desmosomes between keratinocytes
Type VII collagen in anchoring fibrils below the lamina densa
BP180 and BP230 in hemidesmosomes of basal keratinocytes
Tissue transglutaminase in the papillary dermis
Keratin 14 intermediate filaments within basal keratinocytes

questions.explanation_html: Bullous pemphigoid is caused by autoantibodies to hemidesmosomal proteins, especially BP180 and BP230, which anchor basal keratinocytes to the basement membrane. Separation occurs below the epidermis, producing tense bullae. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 along the basement-membrane zone.

wrong_choice_explanations.1: Desmoglein 3 is targeted in pemphigus vulgaris, which causes flaccid bullae and mucosal erosions.
wrong_choice_explanations.2: Type VII collagen is targeted in epidermolysis bullosa acquisita and localizes to the dermal side on salt-split skin.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Tissue transglutaminase is associated with celiac disease; dermatitis herpetiformis has granular IgA at dermal papillae.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Keratin 14 mutations cause inherited epidermolysis bullosa simplex rather than an acquired linear IgG/C3 disorder.

questions.educational_objective: Bullous pemphigoid targets BP180/BP230 hemidesmosomes, causing subepidermal tense bullae and linear IgG/C3 deposition at the basement-membrane zone.

media.alt_text: Original skin-junction schematic showing hemidesmosomes, subepidermal cleavage, and linear IgG/C3 in bullous pemphigoid.

taxonomy.subtopic: Disruption of medial circumflex femoral retinacular branches and osteonecrosis

questions.stem_html: A 74-year-old woman sustains a displaced intracapsular fracture of the femoral neck after a fall. The accompanying vascular diagram shows vessels ascending along the posterior femoral neck. Damage to which vessel most strongly predisposes the femoral head to osteonecrosis?

options.text_html: Lateral circumflex femoral artery transverse branch
Obturator artery branch within the ligament of the head
Inferior gluteal artery
Retinacular branches of the medial circumflex femoral artery
Superior gluteal artery

questions.explanation_html: The main adult blood supply to the femoral head is delivered by retinacular branches of the medial circumflex femoral artery that course along the femoral neck. A displaced intracapsular neck fracture can tear these vessels, causing avascular necrosis and nonunion. The ligamentum teres artery is usually insufficient in adults.

wrong_choice_explanations.1: The lateral circumflex femoral artery contributes to the trochanteric region but is not the dominant supply to the adult femoral head.
wrong_choice_explanations.2: The artery in the ligament of the head is more important in children and usually cannot maintain the adult femoral head alone.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: The inferior gluteal artery supplies gluteal structures and does not provide the principal retinacular supply.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: The superior gluteal artery supplies gluteus medius and minimus rather than the femoral head.

questions.educational_objective: Displaced intracapsular femoral-neck fractures can interrupt medial circumflex femoral retinacular branches, leading to femoral-head osteonecrosis.

media.alt_text: Original hip vascular anatomy schematic showing medial circumflex femoral retinacular branches along the femoral neck.

taxonomy.subsystem: Ischemic heart disease and infarct healing
taxonomy.subtopic: Days 3-7 macrophage-mediated tissue softening and mechanical rupture

questions.stem_html: A 59-year-old man is hospitalized after a large transmural myocardial infarction. On day 5, he develops sudden hypotension and pulseless electrical activity. The accompanying histology timeline shows abundant macrophages removing necrotic myocytes with little mature collagen. Which process most directly created the vulnerable myocardial wall?

options.text_html: Immediate dystrophic calcification of necrotic fibers
Dense type I collagen deposition by mature fibroblasts
Replacement of myocytes by fully organized granulation tissue
Persistent reversible myocyte swelling without membrane disruption
Proteolytic clearance of necrotic tissue before adequate scar formation

questions.explanation_html: During days 3-7 after myocardial infarction, macrophages remove necrotic myocytes and degraded extracellular matrix. The infarct is softest before sufficient collagen is deposited, making free-wall, septal, or papillary-muscle rupture possible. Robust granulation tissue and collagen develop later.

wrong_choice_explanations.1: Dystrophic calcification is a late consequence of tissue injury and does not explain day-5 rupture.
wrong_choice_explanations.2: Dense collagen increases tensile strength and appears later in healing.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Granulation tissue begins at the margins around the end of the first week and is not yet a mature scar.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: By day 5 the infarcted myocytes are irreversibly necrotic rather than reversibly swollen.

questions.educational_objective: Macrophage-mediated removal of necrotic myocardium during days 3-7 precedes adequate collagen deposition, creating the period of greatest mechanical rupture risk.

media.alt_text: Original myocardial-infarction healing timeline highlighting macrophage-dominant tissue softening on days 3-7 before collagen scar formation.

taxonomy.subsystem: Granulomatous bacterial infection and immunomodulator risk
taxonomy.subtopic: TNF-alpha-dependent granuloma maintenance and reactivation during infliximab therapy

questions.stem_html: A 43-year-old man with Crohn disease begins infliximab therapy without latent-tuberculosis screening. Four months later, he develops fever, night sweats, weight loss, and an apical cavitary lung lesion. The accompanying diagram shows disruption of an organized macrophage granuloma. Blockade of which cytokine most directly allowed reactivation?

options.text_html: Tumor necrosis factor alpha
Interleukin 4
Interleukin 5
Interleukin 10
Interleukin 17

questions.explanation_html: TNF-alpha is crucial for recruitment, organization, and maintenance of macrophage-rich granulomas that contain Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Monoclonal anti-TNF agents such as infliximab can disrupt granuloma integrity and permit latent bacilli to proliferate and disseminate. Screening for latent infection is therefore required before therapy.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: IL-4 promotes Th2 differentiation and IgE responses rather than maintenance of tuberculous granulomas.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: IL-5 supports eosinophil growth and activation.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: IL-10 is anti-inflammatory and can suppress macrophage responses, but infliximab specifically blocks TNF-alpha.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: IL-17 contributes to neutrophil recruitment and mucosal inflammation but is not the principal cytokine targeted by infliximab.

questions.educational_objective: TNF-alpha maintains the architecture and antimicrobial function of tuberculous granulomas; anti-TNF therapy can reactivate latent tuberculosis.

media.alt_text: Original schematic showing an apical cavitary lesion and disruption of a TNF-dependent macrophage granuloma during anti-TNF therapy.
